issues.legal_issue: A relaxation rule permitting exceptional mineral-lease grants is not facially invalid for conferring unguided discretion when its purposes and the governing framework provide objective limits and the decision-maker must record reasons.
material_facts: The rule authorized the government to grant or renew a quarry lease, or permit quarrying, on different terms from those in the ordinary rules when it considered that necessary for mineral development and the public interest.
The rule required the government to record its reasons for exercising that power.
The governing mining legislation and rules addressed mineral development, including the scientific exploitation of minerals without waste, and the rule's exercise remained subject to judicial review.
The challenge in the proceedings was to the validity of the rule itself, not to the merits of a particular exercise of the power.
issues.conclusion: The rule was not per se arbitrary or invalid under Article 14; an allegedly improper exercise of the power could be challenged in an individual case.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 14, a discretionary relaxation power is not invalid merely because it is broad if its purposes and the context of the legislation supply objective guidance and the decision-maker must give reasons. Mineral development and public interest have objective content in the context of the mining framework; judicial review provides a safeguard against improper exercises. The Court relied on Sections 2 and 15 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, and on P.J. Irani v. State of Madras, S. Kandaswamy Chettiar v. State of Tamil Nadu, Jalan Trading Co. (P) Ltd. v. Mill Mazdoor Union, and Workmen v. Meenakshi Mills Ltd.

rule.if: facial_validity_challenge and relaxation_rule_exists and rule_requires_recorded_reasons and governing_framework_gives_objective_content

predicates.facial_validity_challenge: A party challenges the validity of a rule authorizing exceptional government action, rather than challenging only a particular decision made under it.
predicates.relaxation_rule_exists: A rule authorizes the government to depart from ordinary requirements for a specified kind of grant or permission.
predicates.rule_requires_recorded_reasons: The rule requires the government to record reasons when it exercises the exceptional power.
predicates.governing_framework_gives_objective_cont: The surrounding legal framework gives objective meaning to the rule's stated purposes and allows review of whether a decision serves them.

issues.definition: When a facial challenge concerns an exceptional power bounded by stated purposes, required reasons, and an objectively informative framework, the rule is not facially invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A relaxation rule need not be read down to permit only changes to individual lease terms when it allows exceptions to other rules and remains consistent with the purpose of the governing legislation.
material_facts: The ordinary rules included policies restricting who could receive certain quarry leases and where quarrying could take place.
The relaxation rule operated notwithstanding the other rules and permitted grants on different terms when considered necessary for mineral development and the public interest, with reasons recorded.
The mining legislation and the rules were directed to mineral development in the public interest, and the government had changed its approach to mineral exploitation over time.
The Court considered whether the relaxation rule had to be limited to varying lease terms and conditions so that it could not make exceptions to other rules.
issues.conclusion: The rule was not required to be read down to apply only to variations in lease terms and conditions; an exception to other rules was not inherently inconsistent with the statutory scheme.
issues.legal_principle: A provision for relaxation or exemption must be assessed in light of its purpose and effect within the statutory scheme. It is valid where it is consistent with the purpose of the governing legislation, rather than rendering that purpose unworkable; provisions should be read harmoniously, but a relaxation power need not be confined merely to preserve every ordinary rule unchanged. Article 14 permits an objectively based departure from a prescribed norm. The Court relied on Section 31 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, Rule 66 of the Karnataka Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1969, S. Kandaswamy Chettiar v. State of Tamil Nadu, Prabhakaran Nair v. State of Tamil Nadu, and Ramana Dayaram Shetty v. International Airport Authority of India.

rule.if: challenge_to_scope_of_relaxation_rule and relaxation_rule_exists and relaxation_serves_governing_purpose and relaxation_does_not_defeat_parent_legislation

predicates.challenge_to_scope_of_relaxation_rule: A party contends that an exception-making rule must be narrowly interpreted to preserve other rules or policies.
predicates.relaxation_rule_exists: A rule authorizes the government to make an exception to ordinary requirements in specified circumstances.
predicates.relaxation_serves_governing_purpose: The exception-making power is directed to furthering the purpose of the governing legal framework.
predicates.relaxation_does_not_defeat_parent_legisl: The exception can operate without making the purpose of the governing legislation unworkable.

issues.definition: Where an exception-making rule advances the governing framework's purpose without defeating it, a challenge to its scope does not require the rule to be read down.

issues.legal_issue: Leases granted under a relaxation rule cannot be cancelled solely because that rule was held invalid when the rule is valid, although the merits of a particular exercise of the power remain reviewable.
material_facts: A lower court cancelled leases granted under the relaxation rule because it had declared that rule invalid.
The Supreme Court held that the rule was not per se invalid.
The Court did not examine whether the government had properly exercised the relaxation power in each individual lease grant and left that question open for challenge on its merits.
issues.conclusion: The cancellations based solely on the rule's supposed invalidity were set aside, without foreclosing challenges to whether the power had been properly exercised in particular cases.
issues.legal_principle: A lease is not invalid merely because it was granted under a rule that was incorrectly held invalid. Whether the government properly exercised the power in a particular case remains open to judicial review on the merits. The Court applied its conclusion on the validity of the relaxation rule under Article 14 and the principles governing judicial review of discretionary state action, including Ramana Dayaram Shetty v. International Airport Authority of India.

predicates.lease_cancellation_review: A court reviews cancellation of a lease granted under an exceptional government power.
predicates.relaxation_rule_is_valid: The rule authorizing the exceptional grant is valid.
predicates.cancellation_based_only_on_rule_invalidi: The lease was cancelled solely because the rule authorizing it had been declared invalid, without a determination that the power was improperly exercised.

issues.definition: When a valid relaxation rule was the only basis for cancelling a lease granted under it, the cancellation is set aside, while any separate challenge to the particular grant remains available.
